record.original_question: For commuting diffeomorphisms f and g of S1 , to what extent we can say that the 2 cycle (f, g) − (g, f ) of BDiff(S1 )δ is a boundary ?

evidence.quote: Question 5.2. For commuting diffeomorphisms f and g of S1 , to what extent we can say that the 2 cycle (f, g) − (g, f ) of BDiff(S1 )δ is a boundary ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathrm{Diff}(S^1)$ denote the group of orientation-preserving smooth diffeomorphisms of the circle, regarded as a discrete group, and let $B\mathrm{Diff}(S^1)^\delta$ denote its classifying space. The group homology $H_*(B\mathrm{Diff}(S^1)^\delta;\mathbb{Z})$ is computed by the bar complex of $\mathrm{Diff}(S^1)$ as a discrete group; in particular, given two elements $f,g\in\mathrm{Diff}(S^1)$, the bar 2-chain $(f,g)-(g,f)$ is a cycle whenever $f$ and $g$ commute (i.e.\ $fg=gf$).

Problem: For commuting diffeomorphisms $f,g\in\mathrm{Diff}(S^1)$, determine to what extent the 2-cycle $(f,g)-(g,f)$ is a boundary in the bar complex of $B\mathrm{Diff}(S^1)^\delta$. More precisely, characterize those commuting pairs $(f,g)$ for which the homology class $[(f,g)-(g,f)]\in H_2(B\mathrm{Diff}(S^1)^\delta;\mathbb{Z})$ vanishes, and identify nontrivial invariants (such as cohomology classes pulled back from $B\mathrm{Diff}(S^1)^\delta$) that detect this class.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research question about the group homology of the discrete diffeomorphism group of the circle. A targeted web search did not return a paper resolving the vanishing or non-vanishing of the antisymmetrized 2-cycle for commuting circle diffeomorphisms; standard references on diffeomorphism group homology (Hatcher's survey, Randal-Williams) do not address this specific question. The status appears open.

status_evidence.title: A 50-Year View of Diffeomorphism Groups (Hatcher)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of diffeomorphism group results; does not resolve the boundary question for the antisymmetric 2-cycle of commuting circle diffeomorphisms.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution found in standard surveys of Diff(S^1) homology.

status_evidence.title: Diffeomorphisms of discs (Randal-Williams)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses homology of diffeomorphism groups via parameterized surgery and embedding calculus, without addressing this specific 2-cycle question.
status_evidence.claim: Modern techniques for homology of Diff are surveyed, but the specific question is not addressed.
